content: {"summary":"The fraud‑scorer rollout in June 2026 caused the pods to use more CPU per request, exceeding their CPU limit and triggering CFS throttling, which in turn produced PAYAPI‑W0310 errors on the payments API.","likely_cause":"CFS throttling caused by the new fraud‑scorer code exceeding the existing CPU limit (limits unchanged, worker count unchanged).","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"The fraud‑scorer deploy increased CPU usage, leading to CFS throttling.","evidence_ids":["INC-0172#0","RB-002#0","RB-002#1"],"quote":"If a service's p99 latency climbs while its CPU graph looks comfortable, suspect CFS throttling before anything else."},{"text":"Worker count and CPU limits were unchanged, so the new code exceeded the existing quota.","evidence_ids":["INC-0172#1","RB-002#3"],"quote":"Pods log `WEB_CONCURRENCY=16` at start, same as before, so 16 workers on each."},{"text":"Docs advise inspecting throttling metrics and raising the CPU limit or adjusting worker count.","evidence_ids":["RB-002#0","RB-002#3"],"quote":"raise the CPU limit for the affected Deployment"}],"next_checks":["Check container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total vs container_cpu_cfs_periods_total in Grafana (throttling mode).","Verify the current CPU limit and request settings for fraud‑scorer pods.","Confirm WEB_CONCURRENCY (or GOMAXPROCS) matches the CPU limit.","Profile the new fraud‑scorer binary to locate extra CPU consumption.","Consider raising the CPU limit or reducing worker count as per RB‑002 guidance."]}
